questions.stem: About plasma, the correct proposition is:
options: It is an intermediate state combining the properties of a liquid and a crystalline solid
It is made up only of neutral atoms and molecules
It is used in mobile telephony screens
It is an ionized gas, called the 4th state of matter
It has its own volume
questions.explanation: Plasma is the 4th state of matter: an ionized gas made of electrons, ions, atoms or neutral molecules. The intermediate state used in mobile telephony is the liquid crystal, not plasma.

options: Has neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume
Is condensed (particles close together) but fluid (particles weakly bound and mobile)
Has strongly bound, immobile particles
Has a free surface that, at rest, follows the curvature of the container
Tends to occupy all the available volume
questions.explanation: A liquid has its own volume, takes the shape of its container, has a flat horizontal free surface at rest, and is condensed but fluid. Having no fixed volume and filling all available space describe the gaseous state.

options: Has its own volume but takes the shape of its container
Is condensed, with particles close together
Is made up of electrons, ions, atoms and neutral molecules
Has a flat, horizontal free surface at rest
Is dispersed and completely disorganized, with almost independent particles
questions.explanation: A gas has neither fixed shape nor volume, fills all available volume, is dispersed and disorganized, and is made only of atoms and molecules. Electrons and ions characterize plasma (an ionized gas).

questions.stem: About energy units, the correct proposition is:
options: 1 erg = 10⁷ J
The erg is the energy unit of the SI (M.K.S.A) system
The joule is the energy unit of the CGS system
questions.explanation: 1 cal = 4.184 J. The joule is the SI unit, the erg is the CGS unit with 1 erg = 10⁻⁷ J (not 10⁷), and 1 eV = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J.

questions.stem: An energy of 2 cal is equal to:
options: 2 J
questions.explanation: 2 cal = 2 × 4.184 = 8.368 J, and since 1 erg = 10⁻⁷ J, 8.368 J = 8.368 × 10⁷ erg. Dividing instead of multiplying gives the 0.478 J and 10⁻⁷ erg traps.

questions.stem: A glass contains oil floating on water (two immiscible liquids). This system has:
options: One phase and one liquid state
Two phases and two liquid states
One phase and two states
Two phases and only one liquid state
A single phase, since both components are liquids
questions.explanation: Two immiscible liquids form two different phases (regions with different properties) but only one state of matter (liquid). Being in the same state does not make them one phase.

questions.stem: About thermodynamic systems, the correct proposition is:
options: An open system exchanges only energy with the surrounding environment
A closed system exchanges only energy with the surrounding environment
A closed system exchanges energy and matter with the surrounding environment
An isolated system exchanges only matter with the surrounding environment
An open glass of milk is an example of an isolated system
questions.explanation: Open: exchanges energy and matter (open glass of milk). Closed: exchanges only energy (sealed jar). Isolated: no exchange at all (thermos flask).

questions.stem: Which pairing of example and system type is correct?
options: Open glass of milk → closed system
Sealed jar of jam → isolated system
Sealed jar of jam → open system
Thermos flask → isolated system
Thermos flask → closed system
questions.explanation: The thermos (ideally) exchanges neither energy nor matter, so it is isolated. The sealed jar exchanges only energy (closed) and the open glass of milk exchanges energy and matter (open).

questions.stem: The saturating vapor pressure (Psat) of a liquid placed in a closed chamber:
options: Depends on the temperature and on the volume of the chamber
Depends on the quantity of liquid introduced
Depends only on the temperature
Is the vapor pressure of a substance in equilibrium with its solid phase
Is reached in an open system
questions.explanation: In a closed chamber at fixed temperature, molecules vaporize until the space is saturated; the pressure reached, Psat, depends only on temperature. It is defined with respect to the liquid phase, not the solid phase.

questions.stem: Once saturation is reached in a closed chamber at fixed temperature:
options: Molecules stop passing from the liquid to the gaseous phase
The vapor pressure keeps rising as long as liquid remains
Adding more liquid to the chamber raises the vapor pressure
The space above the liquid stays at P = 0
The flow of molecules from liquid to gas equals the flow from gas to liquid
questions.explanation: Equilibrium means the liquid→gas flow equals the gas→liquid flow; exchanges continue but cancel out. Because Psat depends only on temperature, adding liquid does not change it.

options: Psat = (t/100)⁴, with Psat in bar and t in °C, valid for 100°C ≤ t ≤ 200°C
Psat = (t/100)⁴, with Psat in Pa and t in K
Psat = (100/t)⁴, with Psat in bar and t in °C
Psat = (t/100)⁴, valid for 0°C ≤ t ≤ 100°C
Psat = (t/100)², with Psat in bar and t in °C
questions.explanation: Duperray: Psat = (t/100)⁴ with Psat in bar and t in °C, for 100°C ≤ t ≤ 200°C. Check: t = 100°C gives 1 bar, the boiling point at atmospheric pressure.

questions.stem: A sealed pressure cooker maintains a water vapor pressure of 2 bar. Using Duperray's formula, the boiling point of water inside is approximately:
questions.explanation: t = 100 × (Psat)^(1/4) = 100 × 2^(1/4) ≈ 119°C. Taking the square root instead gives 141°C, and a linear relation gives 200°C.

questions.stem: About pressure units, the correct proposition is:
options: 1 atm = 101325 mmHg
1 bar = 10⁵ Pa ≈ 1 atm
1 Pa = 7.5 mmHg
The pressure exerted by a column of liquid depends on the cross-section S of the column
The pressure exerted by a column of liquid does not depend on the liquid's density
questions.explanation: 1 bar = 10⁵ Pa ≈ 1 atm = 101325 Pa = 760 mmHg, and 1 Pa = 7.5 × 10⁻³ mmHg. For a liquid column P = ρgh: S cancels out, but density matters.

questions.stem: What height of a water column (ρ = 1 g/cm³, g = 9.81 m/s²) exerts a pressure of 1 atm?
questions.explanation: P = ρgh ⇒ h = 101325 / (1000 × 9.81) ≈ 10.3 m. The 0.76 m value is the mercury column (ρ = 13.6 g/cm³), not water.

questions.stem: A mass m = 4 g of water (M = 18 g/mol) is introduced into an initially empty container of volume V = 10 L and heated to 80°C. Psat(80°C) = 0.466 bar (R = 8.31 SI). What mass of water remains liquid?
options: 0 g (all the water vaporizes)
questions.explanation: The maximum vapor is n = PsatV/RT = 46600 × 0.010 / (8.31 × 353) ≈ 0.159 mol ≈ 2.86 g < 4 g, so saturation is reached and 4 − 2.86 ≈ 1.14 g stays liquid. 2.86 g is the vaporized mass, not the liquid.

questions.stem: (Continued: 4 g of water in the 10 L container.) The container is heated to 100°C, where Psat = 1 bar. The vapor pressure inside is:
options: 1 bar (saturated vapor)
0.82 bar
0.69 bar (all the water is vapor, unsaturated)
0.58 bar
questions.explanation: If all 4 g (0.222 mol) vaporize, P = nRT/V = 0.222 × 8.31 × 373 / 0.010 ≈ 0.69 bar < Psat = 1 bar, so there is no liquid left and the vapor is unsaturated. P only equals Psat if liquid remains.

questions.stem: A mass of 0.5 g of water (M = 18 g/mol) is introduced into an initially empty 10 L container at 80°C, where Psat = 0.466 bar (R = 8.31 SI). The correct proposition is:
options: Saturation is reached and the vapor pressure is 0.466 bar
Part of the water remains liquid
All the water vaporizes and the vapor pressure is about 0.082 bar
The vapor pressure is about 0.82 bar
The vapor pressure depends only on the temperature
questions.explanation: P = nRT/V = (0.5/18) × 8.31 × 353 / 0.010 ≈ 8150 Pa ≈ 0.082 bar < Psat, so all the water vaporizes. The vapor pressure depends only on temperature only when the vapor is saturated.

questions.stem: A sealed 2 L pressure cooker is heated to 120°C. Using Duperray's formula, what maximum mass of water (M = 18 g/mol) can exist as vapor inside? (R = 8.31 SI)
questions.explanation: Psat = (120/100)⁴ ≈ 2.07 bar, so n = PsatV/RT = 207360 × 0.002 / (8.31 × 393) ≈ 0.127 mol ≈ 2.29 g. Using Psat = 1 bar instead gives about 1.10 g.
